newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe's approval rating creeps up in France - poll.
newsitem.headline: Juppe's approval rating creeps up in France - poll.

text.p: Prime Minister Alain Juppe's approval rating in France has crept up from a record low, an opinion poll showed on Wednesday.
The Gallup survey for the weekly L'Express found that 30 percent of 956 people queried on January 9 and 10 approved of Juppe's actions as prime minister against 66 who disapproved.
The figures were an improvement for conservative Juppe on a 25-72 percent split in the last comparable survey in November, the lowest since he took office in May 1995.

Juppe published a book last month pleading for greater understanding of his policies, including austerity to help France qualify for a single European currency. French unemployment is at a post-war high of 12.7 percent.
Juppe has said he wants to stay on until legislative elections in early 1998.
President Jacques Chirac's ratings also picked up in the poll, taken at the end of a political truce over the Christmas and New Year holidays.
Thirty-six percent of those polled said they approved of his actions as president against 52 percent opposed. In November, his rating was 35-56.
